blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Knowledge that a language model appears to forget during finetuning often remains stored and can be recovered, a phenomenon called spurious forgetting. Finetuning on new facts can even produce forgetting that undoes itself: recall of the old facts collapses, recovers as training continues on new facts alone, and only then erodes for good. We seek to understand when such forgetting is not catastrophic. A minimal associative memory reproduces these dynamics with three ingredients: keys with shared structure, concentrated new values, and normalization in the network. Finetuning moves all old representations along a common direction, hiding the old facts while preserving their relative geometry; normalization withdraws this shift once the new facts are learned, whereas fact-specific changes accumulate and cause the erosion. Moreover, subtracting the common shift eliminates the collapse in a Transformer trained on synthetic data, and removing a single direction from each weight update restores old facts in a pretrained language model. Forgetting thus combines a shared, reversible loss of access with a slow erosion of individual facts, and only the second is catastrophic. Which one dominates depends on whether the new data move old memories together or apart.
blocks.zh: 一种语言模型在微调时似乎会被遗忘的知识常常被储存起来,并且可以被恢复,这种现象被称作"虚伪的遗忘". 对新事实的细化甚至可以造成忘记这一点:对旧事实的回忆崩溃,随着仅仅对新事实的培训的继续而恢复,只有这样,才能永远侵蚀。 我们寻求理解,当这种忘记不是灾难性的。 最小的关联内存以三种成分来复制这些动态:共享结构的密钥,集中的新价值和网络中的正常化. 微调将所有旧的表述沿着共同的方向移动,隐藏了旧的事实,同时保留了相对的几何;常态化在了解了新事实后会撤销这一转变,而具体事实的变化则会累积并造成侵蚀. 此外,去掉通俗的移位消除了被合成数据所训练的变形器的倒塌,去掉每个重量更新中的一个单一方向,恢复了预先被训练的语言模型中的旧事实. 因此,遗忘将共同的、可逆转的准入丧失与个别事实缓慢地被侵蚀结合起来,只有第二种是灾难性的。 哪个主导取决于新数据是将旧记忆一起移动还是分开.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Continually training a neural network on new data can severely damage the knowledge and skills it previously acquired, a phenomenon known as catastrophic forgetting ( McCloskey and Cohen, 1989 ; Ratcliff, 1990 ; French, 1999 ) .
It has been reported across many settings, from image classification ( Goodfellow et al., 2014 ; Zenke et al., 2017 ; Ramasesh et al., 2021 ) to deep reinforcement learning ( Kirkpatrick et al., 2017 ; Rolnick et al., 2019 ) , and large language models are no exception ( Luo et al., 2025 ; Zucchet et al., 2025 ; Marek et al., 2026 ) .
Yet, a loss of performance need not be a loss of knowledge: a different prompt can restore lost capabilities ( Kotha et al., 2024 ) , and brief training on a few old examples can undo forgetting that reflects a loss of task alignment rather than of knowledge, named spurious forgetting ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) .
Accuracy measured at a single point in training therefore cannot tell whether knowledge was erased or only hidden. What hides it, and whether training on the new data alone can reveal it again, remains unclear; we ask
blocks.zh:
不断对神经网络进行关于新数据的培训会严重损害它以前获得的知识和技能,这种现象被称为灾难性的遗忘(McCloskey和Cohen,1989年;Ratchliff,1990年;法语,1999年)。
据报道,从图像分类(Goodfellow等,2014年;Zenke等,2017年;Ramasesh等,2021年)到深度强化学习(Kirkpatrick等,2017年;Rolnick等,2019年),大语言模型也不例外(Luo等,2025年;Zucchet等,2025年;Marek等,2026年).
然而,性能的丧失不一定是知识的丧失:不同的瞬间可以恢复失去的能力(Kotha等,2024年),关于几个老例子的简短培训可以消除遗忘,这些例子反映了任务协调的丧失,而不是知识的丧失,这被称为虚伪的遗忘(Zheng等,2025年)。
因此,在单一培训点测得的准确性无法分辨知识是被抹去,还是只被隐藏。 何以掩盖,以及仅就新数据进行培训是否能够再次揭示,这一点仍然不明确;我们问

blocks.en: When is forgetting not catastrophic?
blocks.zh: 什么时候忘记不是灾难性的?

blocks.en:
We study this question for factual knowledge, as forgetting and loss of access can be cleanly disentangled.
How language models store and retrieve facts is well understood ( Geva et al., 2021 ; Meng et al., 2022 ; Geva et al., 2023 ; Nanda et al., 2023 ) , and synthetic biographies ( Allen-Zhu and Li, 2024 ; Zucchet et al., 2025 ) let us specify exactly which facts the model knows, guarantee that the new facts were never seen before, and control how the two relate.
We can then ask not only whether the model still outputs an old fact, but also whether the fact is still stored.
In this setting, finetuning on new facts alone produces spurious forgetting in a particularly clear form (Figure 1 ): recall of the old facts collapses, then recovers as training continues on the same new facts, before a slower decline sets in.
Since there is no replay of the old facts, the recovery can only come from knowledge that survived the collapse.
blocks.zh:
我们研究这个问题是为了了解事实,因为忘记和失去接触的机会可以完全分开。
语言模型如何存储和取回事实得到很好的理解(Geva等,2021;Meng等,2022;Geva等,2023;Nanda等,2023),以及合成传记. (Allen-Zhu and Li, 2024; Zucchet等, 2025.)让我们具体说明模型确切知道哪些事实,保证以前从未见过新的事实,并控制两者之间的关系。
然后,我们不仅可以问这个模型是否仍然输出出一个旧的事实,而且还可以问这个事实是否仍然被存储.
在这个背景下,仅仅对新事实进行微调,就会产生一种特别明确的遗忘(图1):回顾旧事实崩溃,然后随着对同样新事实的继续培训而恢复,然后才开始缓慢下降。
由于旧事实没有再现,恢复只能由在倒塌中幸存下来的知识来进行.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are as follows: – A clean case of spurious forgetting. In a controlled factual-recall setting, finetuning on new facts alone makes recall of the old facts collapse and then return, without any replay, and changing only where the new answers lie turns the same finetuning into steady forgetting. – A minimal mechanism. A minimal associative memory reproduces the phenomenon once three ingredients are present: keys with shared structure, new answers concentrated in one region, and normalization.
Finetuning then moves all old representations together, which hides the old facts without erasing them, and normalization undoes this shift once the new facts are learned.
Changes specific to each fact accumulate and cause a slower, lasting forgetting. – Causal evidence in trained models. In Transformers trained from scratch on synthetic data, removing the common shift eliminates the collapse, whose end is set by the learning of the new facts, not by the number of training steps. In a pretrained language model, recall of the old facts recovers only when the subjects of the new facts reveal nothing about their answers, and removing one direction of each weight update restores it beyond the trained model’s recall at equal new-fact accuracy. Together, our results show that forgetting is not catastrophic when the update moves old memories together rather than apart: the knowledge is then hidden rather than erased, and can be recovered, sometimes by just continuing finetuning for longer.

blocks.en: 2 Forgetting that undoes itself
blocks.zh: 2个 忘记了自己

blocks.en:
To understand when forgetting is not catastrophic, we first need a setting in which it clearly is not: one in which performance collapses, yet the knowledge demonstrably survives (Appendix C.1 ).
We use synthetic biographies ( Allen-Zhu and Li, 2024 ) , on which spurious forgetting was identified ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) , as they let us control what the model knows before finetuning and what it learns during it. A transformer is pretrained on two non-overlapping sets of biographies, A A and B B , in a single stage rather than one per set ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) , until it recalls all of their facts, and is then finetuned on biographies of new individuals, without any replay. We compare two sets of new biographies, C C and B ′ B^{\prime} , which differ only in how they overlap with the old ones.
We describe how they are built, and what overlapping means precisely, in Section 4 ; for now, the only relevant property is that C C overlaps with both A A and B B , while B ′ B^{\prime} overlaps only with B B (Figure 1 , middle).
blocks.zh:
要理解遗忘不是灾难性的,我们首先需要一个环境,它显然不是:一个表现崩溃的场所,然而知识却明显地存活下来(附录C.1 )。
我们使用合成生理学(Allen-Zhu和Li, 2024年), 变压器在A和B两组不重叠的传记片上预先被训练在一个阶段,而不是每集一次(郑等,2025年),直到它回忆起所有的事实,然后被细化为新个人的传记片,而没有任何回放. 我们比较了两套新的传记,即C和B ' B^{\prime',这些传记仅在它们与旧传记的重叠程度上有所不同.
我们在第4节中描述了这些财产的建造方式和重叠的确切含义;目前,唯一相关的财产是C与A A和B重叠,而B ' B^{\prime'只与B重叠(图1,中间)。

blocks.en:
Finetuning on C C yields classical catastrophic forgetting behavior (Figure 1 , left): as the new facts are learned, recall of both A A and B B declines slowly and steadily.
Finetuning on B ′ B^{\prime} barely affects recall of B B , but recall of A A follows a strikingly different trajectory (Figure 1 , right), in three phases that we refer to throughout the paper:
blocks.zh:
对C的微调产生古典的灾难性遗忘行为(图1,左):随着新事实的发现,对A A和B的回忆缓慢而稳定地下降。
对B ' B^{\prime 的微调几乎不会影响对B B 的回忆,但对A的回忆则遵循一个截然不同的轨迹(图1,正确的),分三个阶段,我们在整个文件中都提到:

blocks.en: – Collapse: recall of A A quickly drops, well before the new facts are learned. – Recovery: recall of A A then partially returns as the new facts are acquired, although A A never reappears in training. – Erosion: finally, recall of A A declines slowly and persistently, as in catastrophic forgetting.

blocks.en:
This trajectory raises two questions: why finetuning on B ′ B^{\prime} hides the facts of A A while sparing those of B B , and why the collapse reverses on its own.
Section 3 answers both in a minimal model.
Section 4 then returns to Transformers, and to the biography structure needed for the phenomenon to appear.
blocks.zh:

第3节以最低模式回答这两个问题。
第4节随后回到变形金刚,并回到现象出现所需的传记结构.

blocks.en: 3 A minimal model reveals the mechanism of spurious forgetting
blocks.zh: 3个 一个最小的模型揭示了 虚伪遗忘的机制

blocks.en: Factual recall, including that of synthetic biographies, can be abstracted as an associative memory: each fact maps a key, the subject it is about, to a value, its answer, which the model must retrieve when queried. We show that a minimal associative memory reproduces spurious forgetting once three ingredients are present: keys that share a common structure, new values concentrated in one part of the vocabulary, and a normalization layer. Its learning dynamics then explain the phenomenon: the structure of the data causes the collapse, and normalization drives the recovery. We check each step of this explanation in the model in Appendix B.8 .
blocks.zh: 事实回想(fact recovery),包括合成生平的回想(fact recording),可以被抽象为关联记忆:每一个事实都描绘出一个关键,它所涉及的主题,到一个价值,它的答案,模型在被询问时必须取回. 我们显示,一个最小的关联内存复制了假象,一旦存在三个成分:共享共同结构的密钥,集中在词汇的一部分的新值,以及一个常态层. 它的学习动力学随后解释了这一现象:数据的结构导致崩溃,而正常化则推动复苏. 我们在附录B.8的模型中检查这一解释的每个步骤。

blocks.en: 3.1 Reproducing spurious forgetting in an associative memory model
blocks.zh: 3.1 国家 在关联记忆模型中产生虚假的遗忘

blocks.en: Many phenomena of factual recall, such as how many facts a model can store as a function of its size ( Allen-Zhu and Li, 2025 ; Nichani et al., 2025 ) , how its loss scales ( Cabannes et al., 2024 ) or the dynamics with which facts are learned ( Zucchet et al., 2025 ; Zucchet et al., 2026 ) , can be reproduced in a simple feedforward associative memory, which strips away the sequence-modeling layers of the transformer.
blocks.zh: 许多事实召回现象,如一个模型可以存储多少个事实作为其大小的函数(Allen-Zhu and Li,2025;Nichani等,2025.),其损失尺度(Cabannes等,2024.)或了解事实的动态(Zucchet等,2025.;Zucchet等,2026.)如何被简单回馈的关联记忆所复制出,从而剥去变压器的序列模型层.

Each key is associated with a value y i y_{i} , a token from a vocabulary of size V V that we split into two halves. The old facts form two sets, A A , whose values are drawn uniformly from one half, and B B , whose values are drawn from the other. blocks.en:
Intuitively, a gradient step on a new fact moves not only its own hidden state but that of every key resembling its own. All keys share a common component, so whatever the updates of the new facts have in common is written into all hidden states at once, the more so as α \alpha grows.
The result is a common shift that leaves the relative geometry of the hidden states mostly intact but, through the readout, favors the half of the vocabulary that contains the new answers, so that the facts of A A can no longer be decoded.

结果是一种常见的转变,使得隐藏状态的相对几何大多完好无损,但通过读出,偏好包含新答案的半个词汇,这样A的事实就不能再被解码了.

The common shift hides the facts of A A . The collapse of A A is a direct consequence of this common shift.
Ignoring normalization for a moment, shifting all hidden states by the same vector adds the same bias to the logits of every old fact, favoring the half of the vocabulary that contains the new answers.
The facts of A A , whose answers lie in the other half, therefore lose to the new answers.
Normalization amplifies this effect.
Once the shift accounts for most of the norm of the hidden states, normalizing rotates all of them toward the shift direction: the old states become more similar to one another, the part of each state that encodes the fact’s own answer is scaled down, and the predictions follow the shift toward the answers most common among the new facts. The facts of B B , whose answers lie in the favored half, are largely spared by the shift itself, which raises the answers of their half roughly together, in proportion to how often each is a new answer: removing the shift from their hidden states barely changes their recall, whereas it restores that of A A .
As their answers are also those of the new facts, they are instead exposed to the fact-specific learning of the new facts, which erodes them steadily, mostly after the collapse (Section 3.3 ).

blocks.en: 3.3 Normalization drives recovery
blocks.zh: 3.3 正常化推动复苏

blocks.en:
Early in finetuning, all hidden states are pushed in the same direction, and this common shift causes the collapse of A A .
Because the normalization fixes the norm of each hidden state, the growing shift comes at the expense of the individual parts, which encode each fact’s own information and eventually become negligible.
At first, this also helps the new facts, whose individual parts point to wrong answers.
However, once the model has learned their individual associations, the shift drowns these as well and prevents the model from predicting the new facts correctly.
Finetuning then undoes the shift, both on the new facts and on the old facts, restoring the individual parts of every hidden state.
For the facts of A A , these still carry most of the information that distinguishes them from one another, and the readout weights of their answers are barely changed by finetuning, as they only receive gradient while the model still puts probability on these answers for the new facts.
The facts of A A can therefore be read out again, and their recall partially recovers.

The shared margin only matters in the first steps of finetuning.

The facts of A A are hidden, not erased. Undoing the common shift only restores the facts of A A if what distinguishes them from one another has survived, and it does, for two reasons.

This individual displacement stays small during the collapse: while the mean of the old hidden states moves a lot, their relative geometry barely changes (Figure 3 , left). The facts of A A therefore keep their ordering within their own half, and even at the bottom of the collapse most of them still rank their correct answer first among the answers of that half (Appendix B.8 ).
Second, the readout weights of the answers of A A receive little gradient: they are only updated while the model puts probability on these answers for the new facts, which stops early in finetuning.
Removing the part of the update that acts on the shared direction, Δ ​ W 1 ​ ( t ) ​ μ ​ μ ⊤ \Delta W_{1}(t)\,\mu\mu^{\top} , while keeping everything else, including the finetuned readout, restores their recall almost entirely (Figure 13 ).
The collapse is thus a loss of access to the facts of A A , not a loss of the facts themselves.

The individual displacements nonetheless keep accumulating after the collapse, and they are not neutral: each old hidden state drifts toward the answers of the new facts whose keys overlap most with its own.
For A A , restoring the mean hidden state therefore helps less and less as finetuning proceeds, and recovery remains incomplete.
For B B , whose answers are those of the new facts, this drift, together with the readout weights of their half, which are refit to the new facts, erodes recall throughout finetuning, and removing the common shift barely helps.

然而,个人流离失所现象在崩溃后不断累积,而且不是中立的:每一个旧的隐蔽状态都转向新事实的答案,而这些新事实的钥匙与其自身最相重叠。
因此,随着收益的微调,平均隐藏状态的恢复会越来越少,而恢复工作仍未完成。
BB的答案是新事实的答案,这种漂移加上他们一半的读取权重,这些权重是对新事实的再现,在整个微调过程中侵蚀了记忆,而去除共同的转变几乎没有什么帮助。

blocks.en: 4 The mechanism in a controlled Transformer
blocks.zh: 页:1 控制变形器中的机制

blocks.en: Having identified the mechanism behind spurious forgetting in a minimal model, we now return to the Transformer of Figure 1 and test whether its collapse and recovery follow the mechanism of the minimal model, first by showing that its data meet the same conditions, then through measurements and interventions on its representations. Table 1 lists where each analysis is repeated across models.
blocks.zh: 在确定了在最小模型中被遗忘的虚假机制之后,我们现在回到图1的变形器,并测试其崩溃和恢复是否遵循最小模型机制,首先表明其数据符合同样条件,然后通过对其表述的测量和干预。 表1列出了每个模型重复分析的情况。

blocks.en: 4.1 Training Transformers on synthetic biographies meets the conditions
blocks.zh: 4.1 对变形器进行合成传记培训符合条件

blocks.en:
The minimal model identifies three conditions for spurious forgetting: a normalization layer, keys that share structure, and new answers concentrated in one region of the output space.
The first condition is met by any Transformer, as every residual block contains a normalization layer ( Vaswani et al., 2017 ) .
In the pre-normalization architecture we use ( Radford et al., 2019 ; Xiong et al., 2020 ) , the last one sits just before the readout.
The other two are properties of the data, which we now describe.
The synthetic biographies of Section 2 ( Allen-Zhu and Li, 2024 ; Zucchet et al., 2025 ) describe a large population of fictitious individuals, each with a unique name and a few attributes, such as a hometown or an employer.
Each fact is stated by filling templates shared across all individuals, such as The hometown of [name] is [city] (Figure 4 , left), and each set of biographies, A A , B B , B ′ B^{\prime} or C C , contains its own individuals, so that the new facts are about individuals the model has never seen.
If we view the feedforward layers of a Transformer as an associative memory in which part of the context serves as the key and the next token as the value ( Geva et al., 2021 ) , the key of a fact is the name of the individual together with the attribute being queried, and its value is the answer.
As all facts about a given attribute are queried in a similar way, their keys share structure by design, just as the keys of the minimal model share the component μ \mu .
The last condition is not present by default, so we build it into the data: we split the possible answers of each attribute at random into two subsets.
The individuals of A A draw their answers from the first subset and those of B B from the second.
The finetuning sets therefore overlap with the old sets through their answers alone: those of B ′ B^{\prime} draw their answers from the second subset, like B B , and those of C C from both subsets. Details of the data and the model are given in Appendix A.1 .

blocks.en: 5 The collapse in a pretrained language model
blocks.zh: 页:1 预训语言模型的崩溃

blocks.en: The controlled transformer meets the conditions of the minimal model by construction while a pretrained language model does not. We can still choose new facts whose answers the old facts never use, but the structure its keys share was set by pretraining on real text, so nothing guarantees that finetuning writes a common shift, or that it later withdraws it. The minimal model makes a prediction for each. The shift should be withdrawn only once the new facts have nothing left in common that helps predict their answers, so that each must be learned on its own; we test this with two kinds of new facts, one that meets this condition and one that does not. And since the shift of the hidden states is written by a single direction of the weight update, the one along which all new facts write together (Section 3.3 ), removing the top direction of each weight update should bring the old facts back.
blocks.zh: 受控变压器通过构造满足了最小型号的条件,而被预先训练的语言型号则没有. 我们仍然可以选择新事实,而旧事实的答案从未使用过,但其密钥共享的结构是通过对真实文本的预训设定的,因此没有任何东西可以保证微调写出一个共同的转变,或者说它后来会撤销. 最小的模型对每一个都做了预测. 只有在新事实没有共同之处有助于预测答案时,才应撤销这种转变,这样,每个事实都必须靠自己来学习;我们用两种新事实来检验这一点,一种符合这个条件,另一种不符合这个条件。 而由于隐藏状态的转变是由重量更新的单一方向来写成的,所有新事实一起写在一起的这个方向(第3.3节),去掉每个重量更新的顶端方向应该能把旧事实带回来.

blocks.en: 5.1 The collapse persists, and reverses when the new facts are arbitrary
blocks.zh: 5.1 联合国 当新的事实具有任意性时,倒行逆施。

blocks.en: OLMo 2 1B ( Team OLMo et al., 2025 ) knows far more facts than we can track, so we take as old facts the CounterFact facts ( Meng et al., 2022 ) it answers correctly before finetuning; they play the role of A A (Appendix A.2 ). We then finetune it without replay on documents stating new facts about people or products, in two separate runs with two kinds of new facts. In both, no new answer shares its first token with the answer of a tracked old fact, so the new answers occupy a region of the output space those old facts do not use, as the answers of B ′ B^{\prime} do for A A . The two kinds differ in what their subjects say about their answers (Section 3.3 ). Synthetic individuals, invented names that receive real companies, cities, countries and languages at random, say nothing: as in the minimal model, the shared direction helps them reach the region of their answers, but not choose within it. Real entities, products from EntityQuestions ( Sciavolino et al., 2021 ) whose manufacturer the model does not know, say something: the kind of product hints at the kind of manufacturer, as a car model hints at a carmaker, so the shared direction keeps helping within the region.
blocks.zh: OLMo 2 1B(Team OLMo等,2025年)对事实的了解远多于我们所能追踪的事实,所以我们把"反事实"(Meng等,2022年)作为旧事实,在微调前正确回答;它们扮演A的角色(Appendix A.2. 然后我们微调一下,不重复说明关于人或产品的新事实的文件,分成两个不同的事实和两种新事实。 在这两个方面,没有一个新的答案与跟踪的旧事实的答案相同,所以新的答案占据了输出空间的一个区域,这些旧事实没有使用,正如B ' B^{\prime}的答案为A A所做的那样。 这两种情况在主体对其答案的看法上有所不同(第3.3节)。 合成个体,发明了随机接收真实公司,城市,国家和语言的名字,毫不留情地说出:如同在最小模式中,共享方向帮助他们到达答案所在的区域,但不在其中选择. 真正的实体,来自实体问题(Sciavolino et al., 2021年)的产品,而模型的制造商并不知道,说一些事情:产品暗示制造商的类型,作为汽车模型暗示汽车制造商,所以共享方向在区域内不断帮助.

blocks.en: With both kinds of new facts, recall of the old facts first rises slightly, although none of them is replayed: finetuning on documents that state facts makes the model favor answers over other continuations, which fixes old facts it already ranked correctly among the possible answers (Appendix D.1 ). With synthetic individuals, the trajectory of the controlled settings then reappears (Figure 5 , left): recall of the old facts collapses before almost any new fact is recalled, recovers as the new facts are learned, and then erodes. More new facts delay the recovery, as each drives its own association with weight 1 / n B 1/n_{B} (Section 3.3 ): with a four times larger set of individuals, the collapse lasts longer and goes deeper (Figure 5 , right). With real entities, the old facts never recover and keep declining even after every new fact is recalled: the shared direction keeps helping the new facts choose their answers within the region, so the shift is never withdrawn.

blocks.en: 5.2 Removing one direction of the update restores the old facts
blocks.zh: 5.2 国家 移除更新的一个方向可以恢复旧事实

blocks.en: In the controlled Transformer, we removed the common shift from the hidden states and logits of the old facts, which were all queried in the same way. In a pretrained model, the old facts are queried through varied prompts, at varied positions, so there is no single set of states over which to average, whereas the weights write the shift whatever the prompt. We therefore act on the weights. In the minimal model, the part of the update that all new facts share is rank-one, written along the shared key direction (Equation 3 ), and it initially dominates the update, while the errors of the new facts are aligned. In a deep network it need not be rank-one at any single layer, but it should still initially dominate each weight update, and thus concentrate in its top singular direction. In the minimal model and in both controlled Transformers, removing this direction indeed restores the old facts at the bottom of the collapse, and what it removes is aligned with the common shift (Appendices B.10 and D.3 ). We therefore subtract the top singular component of the update of every weight matrix in the Transformer blocks of the language model, or, as a control, a random rank-one matrix of the same norm, and evaluate the edited model (Appendix D.2 ).
blocks.zh: 在被控制的"变形器"中,我们从隐藏的状态和旧事实的日志中删除了共同的转变,这些都以同样的方式被质疑. 在一个预先训练过的模型中,旧事实通过各种提示,在不同的位置被问到,因此没有一套可以平均衡量的单一状态,而权重则写着无论什么提示的转变。 因此,我们采取行动。 在最小模式中,更新中所有新事实共享的部分是一等一等,按照共享的关键方向(第3等)来写出,它最初主导了更新,而新事实的错误则是对齐的. 在一个深层的网络中,它不需要在任何单层上排行一等,但最初它仍应主导每个重量更新,从而集中在它的顶端单数方向上. 在最小的模型和两个被控制的变形器中,去掉这个方向确实恢复了倒塌底部的旧事实,它去掉的东西与共同的变相一致(附录B.10和D.3). 因此,我们减去语言模型变形器块中每个重量矩阵更新的上单数部分,或者作为控制,同一规范的随机排名一矩阵,并评价被编辑的模型(附录D.2.).

blocks.en: The edit largely removes the collapse (Figure 5 , middle), whereas the random control leaves recall exactly where training left it (Appendix D.2 ). With synthetic individuals, only the slow erosion remains. With real entities, the edit restores most of the old facts that training never brought back: their steady decline was mostly a shift that was never withdrawn, not erasure. The removed direction also lowers recall of the new facts, but the edit does not rewind finetuning: once the new facts are partly learned, the edited model recalls more old facts than the trained model did at the same accuracy on the new facts (Appendix D.2 ).
blocks.zh: 编辑基本去除倒塌(图5,中段),而随机控制叶则精确地回想起训练离开的地方(附录D.2. 随着合成个体的出现,只有缓慢的侵蚀残留. 有了真正的实体,编辑恢复了大多数训练从未带回的旧事实:它们的平稳下降大多是从未被撤销的转变,而不是去除. 被删除的方向也降低了对新事实的回想,但编辑时并没有倒回微调:一旦部分了解了新事实,被编辑的模型会比训练过的模型在新事实上同样准确地回忆出更多的旧事实(Appendix D.2.

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en:
That a loss of performance need not be a loss of knowledge is an old idea: psychology separates stored from accessible information ( Tulving and Pearlstone, 1966 ; Ebbinghaus, 1885 ) , and suppressed associations return once interference stops ( Postman et al., 1968 ) .
Connectionist networks show the same savings, and training them on unrelated associations can even restore forgotten ones ( Hetherington and Seidenberg, 1989 ; Hinton and Plaut, 1987 ; Harvey and Stone, 1996 ; Atkins and Murre, 1998 ) .
In deep networks, linear probes often recover old tasks that the outputs no longer solve, a phenomenon called shallow forgetting ( Murata et al., 2020 ; Davari et al., 2022 ; Hess et al., 2024 ; Lanzillotta et al., 2026 ) ; performance drops sharply at the start of a new task before returning with some replay ( De Lange et al., 2023 ; Zucchet et al., 2025 ) ; and language models recover lost capabilities with a different prompt ( Kotha et al., 2024 ) or a few old examples, a case named spurious forgetting ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) .
In the settings we identify, the finetuning that hides the old facts also restores them, without probe, prompt or replay, through a shared shift that normalization withdraws once the new facts are learned. This shift towards the new answers may be one concrete form of the loss of task alignment that Zheng et al. (2025) identify behind spurious forgetting.
blocks.zh:
性能的丧失不必是知识的丧失,这是一个旧观念:心理学将存储的信息与可获得的信息相分离(Tulving and Pearlsone, 1966; Ebtheaus, 1885), 被压制的社团一旦干扰停止就会回归(Postman等, 1968.).
联系网络也显示出同样的节省,在无关的协会方面对其进行培训甚至可以恢复被遗忘的协会(Hetherington and Seidenberg,1989;Hinton and Plaut,1987;Harvey and Stone,1996;Atkins and Murre,1998)。
在深层网络中,线性探测器往往会回收输出不再解决的旧任务,这种现象被称作浅忘(Murata等,2020年;Davari等,2022年;Hess等,2024年;Lanzillotta等,2026年;在新任务开始时,性能会急剧下降,然后再进行一些回放(De Lange等,2023年;Zucchet等,2025年;语言模型会回收失去的能力,瞬间(Kotha等,2024年)或几个老例子,一个叫作"假忘"的案件(郑等,2025年)。
在我们确定的背景中,隐藏旧事实的微调也通过共同的转变来恢复旧事实,而无需探测,即时或回放,一旦了解了新的事实,正常化就会撤回。 这种向新答案的转变可能是郑等人丧失任务协调的具体形式. (2025年) 识别背后虚假遗忘.

blocks.en:
Forgetting is usually measured as a single quantity that grows with training, whereas our results suggest two processes on different timescales: a loss of access shared by all old facts, set by what the new data have in common, and a slower erosion specific to each fact.
The pretrained model also points to a trade-off between learning new facts quickly and recovering old ones. When the subjects of the new facts share something that predicts their answers, as the kind of a product predicts the kind of its manufacturer, the shared direction helps the model learn them, and they are learned faster. But for the same reason the shift along this direction keeps helping the new facts, so it is never withdrawn, and the old facts stay hidden. What helps a model generalize to new facts may thus be what keeps it from recovering the old ones.
blocks.zh:
遗忘通常被测量为随着培训而增长的单一数量,而我们的结果则表明在不同的时间尺度上有两个过程:失去所有旧事实所共有的、由新数据所设定的共同内容,以及每个事实所特有的缓慢侵蚀。
预先训练好的模型也指出了快速学习新事实和收复旧事实之间的取舍. 当新事实的主体分享一些预言他们答案的东西时,当一种产品预测其制造商的种类时,共享的方向帮助模型学习它们,它们被学习得更快. 但出于同样的原因,沿着这个方向的转变不断帮助新的事实,所以它永远不会被撤回,而旧的事实仍然被隐藏. 因此,什么有助于模式对新事实的概括,是什么使其无法恢复旧事实。

blocks.en: Limitations. Our minimal model is deliberately extreme, and normalization-driven recovery is likely weaker on real data, although the collapse may be more general. In the pretrained model, we attribute the difference in recovery to what the subjects reveal about their answers, but the two kinds of new facts also differ in other ways, and we study a single model.
blocks.zh: 限制。 我们的最小模式是故意极端的,而正常化驱动的复苏在真实数据上可能较弱,尽管崩溃可能更为普遍. 在被预先训练的模型中,我们把恢复的区别归结为被试者所揭示的答案,但这两种新事实在其他方面也有不同,我们研究了一个单一的模型.

(30) Early in finetuning, both terms survive the average, for two reasons that both come from the structure of the data: – The new answers all lie in the same region. Up to the variations of the prefactor d / ∥ h b ∥ \sqrt{d}/\lVert h_{b}\rVert across new facts, the first term is proportional to W 2 ⊤ ​ ( p ¯ B − q B ) W_{2}^{\top}(\bar{p}_{B}-q_{B}) , where p ¯ B \bar{p}_{B} is the average prediction on the new facts and q B = 1 n B ​ ∑ b 𝟏 y b q_{B}=\frac{1}{n_{B}}\sum_{b}\mathbf{1}_{y_{b}} the distribution of their answers. All new answers belong to the same half of the vocabulary, so q B q_{B} puts all its mass on that half. At the beginning of finetuning, the model has no reason to favor this half for the new keys: it was pretrained on answers from both halves, and its predictions for unseen keys spread over both. p ¯ B − q B \bar{p}_{B}-q_{B} therefore has a large component that moves probability mass from one half to the other, and this component is the same for all new facts. By contrast, which answer is correct within the half, and which wrong answer the model predicts, change from one new fact to the other and cancel in the average. When the new answers are drawn from the whole vocabulary, q B q_{B} and p ¯ B \bar{p}_{B} spread their mass over the two halves in a similar way and this component largely disappears, which is why the collapse does too (Figure 2 , panel 2). – The new facts are confidently wrong. At the same time, all new hidden states contain the shared component α ​ W 1 ​ μ \sqrt{\alpha}\,W_{1}\mu . Rehearsing a subset of old associations can restore the others ( Hinton and Plaut, 1987 ) .
We replay a fixed random subset of the old facts in every finetuning batch of 32 new facts and measure the old facts that are never replayed (Figure 18 ).
Replaying 16 of the 128 old facts lifts their trough from 0.17 0.17 to 0.50 0.50 , as the replayed facts push back on the shift that all old facts share, but raises their final accuracy only from 0.54 0.54 to 0.62 0.62 : erosion is specific to each fact and is barely affected by replaying others.

Where the shift is written. Restoring groups of weights as in Appendix C.4 , the MLP weights and the
attention value and output weights each carry about half of the common shift at the bottom of the collapse ( 46 % 46\% and 47 % 47\% ), the query and key weights 3 % 3\% , and the embedding and LayerNorms less than 2 % 2\% each. Both MLP and attention value and output weights write content into the residual stream, so the shift is again written into the associative memories of the network rather than into where attention goes. Adding MLP blocks does not move
the shift to a new place, but spreads it over a second memory: the update that all new facts share is written wherever the network stores associations, in proportion to how much each store takes part in learning them. The query and key weights, which decide where attention goes, contribute little during the collapse and somewhat more after the recovery, as in the attention-only Transformer, where their share also grows once the fact-specific drift dominates. The collapse is thus a change in what the network writes about each fact, not in which tokens it reads.

blocks.en:
Timing. Changing the learning rate and the batch size as in Appendix C.2 moves the bottom of the collapse from step 20 to step 56, while the new facts are recalled with 23 23 to 33 % 33\% accuracy at every bottom (Figure 26 ). As in the attention-only Transformer, the end of the collapse follows the learning of the new facts rather than the number of steps: a faster optimizer reaches the bottom sooner, but at almost the same point in learning the new facts. This point is not shared across architectures, however: with MLP blocks, the
collapse ends when fewer new facts are recalled than without them. What the two models have in common is therefore not a threshold on new-fact accuracy, but the mechanism that sets it, the individual margin of the new facts turning positive, whose relation to accuracy depends on the model and, as Appendix C.3 shows, on the number of new facts. The depth of the collapse, in contrast, depends on the learning rate, more strongly than without MLP blocks: halving it leaves only a shallow collapse, consistent with Section 4 ,
where the depth, unlike the timing, lies outside our gradient-flow analysis.
